approvedBy: User approval of the Contact / RFQ page
rules: Do not redesign the approved Contact / RFQ page or independently restyle its locked shared components.
Preserve the current RFQ form, validation, file-upload interface, responsive layout, product selector, contact information and configuration architecture.
Keep the honest unconfigured behavior and exact visible status: Request checked, not sent.
Do not simulate a successful submission, silently discard an RFQ or clear buyer input after validation or delivery failure.
Do not implement SMTP, email APIs, Resend, SendGrid or another external email service at this stage.
Before production, connect the RFQ form to a real server-side delivery system and perform a real submission test to the configured inquiry recipient.
Keep product options derived from the existing catalog family data rather than maintaining a second product taxonomy.

Keep the user-approved business display name and catalog-confirmed Eric Huang, email and phone values configurable through the recorded environment variables; the brand update does not verify a new registered legal entity.
Do not add an unverified address, map, contact channel, office, branch, business hour or response-time promise.
Do not add MOQ, lead-time, sample-time, load, tolerance, certification, payment, shipping-time or other unsupported technical or commercial claims.
Keep the current accepted file formats and 10 MB client limit aligned with the future receiving endpoint; narrow both together if production support differs.
A future server-side delivery connection may replace only the configured delivery boundary and must preserve this locked page composition and failure honesty.
